briefdescription.para: Intrusive doubly-linked list used exclusively for Graph node lists.

detaileddescription.para: Provides generic_graph_node_list and generic_graph_node_list_iterator, together with concrete type aliases for mutable and const graph node lists.

simplesect.para: The code in this file is highly EXPERIMENTAL. The APIs will probably change.

sect3.title: Design notes
sect3.para: The list is intrusive: the next/previous pointers live inside the node itself (via T::next_in_graph(size_t)), so no external allocation is needed and iterating is cache-friendly.

Forward and reverse iteration are handled uniformly by a single iterator class parameterised on a direction index (kNextDirection / kPrevDirection). A "before-first-element" sentinel node is always present, which means reverse iterators physically point to the element they logically denote — there is no off-by-one behaviour as with standard std::reverse_iterator.

sect3.title: Requirements on the element type T

listitem.para: T* next_in_graph(size_t direction) — returns the neighbouring node in the given direction; used by the iterator to advance.
void destroy() — removes T from the list and deallocates it.

sect3.para: In practice T is always Node or const Node. destroy() semantics must be renegotiated before this template is used with any other type.
